diagnosis.summary: A traffic spike is hitting all four services simultaneously. Request rates have risen between 3.8x and 9x above baseline across product-service, cart-service, order-service, and payment-service. Error rates on the measured services remain at zero, so the stack is currently absorbing the load.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad traffic surge across all services is the most likely root cause, with no measured errors at this time.
evidence: Request rates rose sharply on every service: product-service from 14.98 to 57.23 rps (3.8x), cart-service from 2.05 to 13.92 rps (6.8x), order-service from 2.97 to 17.68 rps (6.0x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 8.52 rps (9.0x).
product-service DynamoDB read capacity rose from 449.3 to 1717.5 RCU/min, a 3.8x increase consistent with the product-service request rate rise.
cart-service DynamoDB write capacity rose from 122.8 to 835 WCU/min, a 6.8x increase.
order-service DynamoDB write capacity rose from 56.6 to 511 WCU/min (9.0x) and read capacity rose from 60.8 to 275 RCU/min (4.5x).
5xx error rates for product-service and cart-service remain at 0, unchanged from their baseline of 0.
recommended_actions: Monitor all four services closely for any rise in error_rate_5xx or p95_latency_ms, as the stack is currently absorbing the load but capacity headroom is being consumed.
Check lambda_throttle_count on all services; a shared account concurrency limit could be approached under sustained load at these elevated rates.
Watch product-service db_consumed_read_capacity and read_throttle_events, as read capacity has already risen to 1717.5 RCU/min under this spike.
Determine whether the traffic surge is expected (a promotion, a client retry loop, or an external event) before making configuration changes.
If errors begin to rise, apply rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to protect the stack while the traffic source is investigated.
